then.text: Pipits everywhere, thanks to you and a helicopter and a lot of rat bait. We counted them on the survey and I may have cried into a spreadsheet.
A Tussipit, in the tussac, singing! The world's most southerly songbird, back from the rats. We've been waiting years for good news like this. Take these, you've earned them.

else.text: Come back when you've a Tussipit in the Fieldbook. Bring me the proof or at least a decent photograph.
KEP Research Station: the British Antarctic Survey's base here. We study fish, krill, seals and the odd fisheries boat. Rats used to be the problem. The rats are gone.

If you see a plain brown bird in the tussac grass singing its heart out, that's a pipit. If you've caught one, the field ranger at Salisbury Plain will want to hear about it. Ask her to tell you how many we've counted.
